questions.question: Give three (3) organisational standards that commonly apply to the presentation of espresso coffee beverages.
guidance: Presented according to house standard recipe unless requested otherwise by customer
Visually appealing with no drips and spills
Garnished and decorated as per coffee type requirement
Service-ware clean and without chips or cracks
answer_points: Presented according to house standard recipe unless requested otherwise by customer
Visually appealing with no drips and spills
Garnished and decorated as per coffee type requirement
Service-ware clean and without chips or cracks
Served promptly after production

questions.question: How should coffee beans be stored to optimise shelf life?
guidance: Protected from air, sun, heat, and light in an airtight container

Not under refrigerated storage

questions.question: What is the best way to store ground coffee to optimise its shelf life?

questions.question: What size should the coffee tamper be for quality tamping?
guidance: Coffee tampers come in different sizes. A general guideline would be to choose a tamper that is just slightly smaller than the basket used for the coffee grounds.
answer_points: Coffee tampers come in different sizes. A general guideline would be to choose a tamper that is just slightly smaller than the basket used for the coffee grounds.

questions.question: What are the two common types of tampers?
guidance: Flat tampers have a flat base and come in different sizes
Convex tampers have curved base that matches the shape of the basket
answer_points: Flat tampers have a flat base and come in different sizes
Convex tampers have curved base that matches the shape of the basket

questions.question: What size range do filter baskets come in for single shots/doses?
answer_points: Capacities of 7 to 12 grams

questions.question: What size range do filter baskets come in for double shots/doses?
answer_points: Capacities f 14 to 24 grams

questions.question: What does ‘purging the steam wand’ mean?
guidance: The process of releasing a burst of steam from the steam wand on an espresso machine, usually before and after texturing milk to make sure the steam wand is clean and free of any milk residues.
answer_points: The process of releasing a burst of steam from the steam wand on an espresso machine, usually before and after texturing milk to make sure the steam wand is clean and free of any milk residues.

questions.question: Why is it important to ‘purge the steam wand’?
guidance: It is important to remove any milk residues to ensure good quality of texture and taste of the milk prepared for the espresso beverage.
answer_points: It is important to remove any milk residues to ensure good quality of texture and taste of the milk prepared for the espresso beverage.

To remove debris from previous extraction

To remove debris from previous extraction
